sections.h2: Where is Hobbs, and how does the city connect to the rest of Lea County?
sections.html:
Hobbs is in eastern Lea County, less than 4 miles west of the Texas border, and it is the principal city of the Hobbs micropolitan area, which covers all of Lea County. The 2020 census counted 40,508 residents, up from 34,122 in 2010, which Wikipedia says makes it the seventh most populous city in New Mexico.

US 62/180 runs through town, leading east 29 miles to Seminole, Texas, and west 69 miles to Carlsbad. NM 18 runs northwest 21 miles to Lovington, the county seat, and south 61 miles to Kermit, Texas. The city covers 26.4 square miles. Lea County Regional Airport has one commercial passenger airline, and the Texas and New Mexico Railway carries freight.

Hobbs began as a homestead in 1907 and became an oil town after the Midwest Oil Company found oil in 1927. A refinery opened the next year, and the town incorporated in 1929. At the peak of that first boom more than 12,000 people lived there.

The Depression ended the boom for a time. Oil prices fell and the population dropped to about 3,000 by 1931, then climbed back to about 14,000 by 1940 as drilling picked up. A Hobbs Army Airfield was built in 1942, and in 1948 the city bought the air base and turned it into the Hobbs Industrial Air Park, still used for soaring competitions.

That swing from 12,000 to 3,000 and back is worth keeping in mind. The population here has followed oil activity, and an owner who bought near a peak may want to sell in a quieter year. More recently, the Energy Information Administration reports that Lea and Eddy counties together accounted for nearly 1.0 million barrels a day, or 52 percent, of U.S. crude oil production growth between 2020 and 2024.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers and what does that mean for housing?
sections.html:
Wikipedia lists mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction as the largest industries in Hobbs, followed by retail trade and educational services. Nearby Eunice hosts a uranium enrichment facility operated by Urenco USA, which provides technician and nuclear engineering jobs across the region, including Hobbs.

Other anchors include Hobbs Municipal Schools, the University of the Southwest, a private four-year Christian university, and New Mexico Junior College, a public two-year college that opened in 1966. Zia Park, a racetrack and casino with a 154-room hotel, is in town, and the Soaring Society of America has its headquarters here.

  • Oil and gas extraction is the largest industry, so local demand is tied to energy activity.
  • Schools, colleges and retail add employment that does not depend on drilling.
  • The Urenco enrichment plant in nearby Eunice draws technical workers to the area.

Ask any buyer or agent how current oilfield activity is affecting demand in your part of town.

sections.h2: What flood and weather risks should a Hobbs seller disclose to a buyer?
sections.html:
The City of Hobbs says flooding is one of the biggest hazards in the greater Hobbs area and can happen with little or no notice. It also lists severe weather, extreme heat and drought, grass fires and power outages as hazards.

The city has taken part in the National Flood Insurance Program and the Community Rating System since 1992. It is a Class 8 community, which the city says saves residents 10 percent on flood insurance premiums. If a flood zone touches a property line, the city notes that insurance may be cheaper, though not required. Land drains east toward Seminole Draw or southeast toward Monument Draw, so water follows the low points.

Hobbs also keeps copies of elevation certificates, which a buyer may need for insurance if the house sits in a Special Flood Hazard Area. The Engineering Department can be reached at (575) 397-9232. The city's page also says that thunderstorms, hail, lightning, tornadoes and wind-driven grass fires happen on the high plains. Summer highs average in the mid 90s, and annual precipitation is about 12 inches by the city's count, close to the 13.77 inches NOAA reports.

Gather these before listing:

  • FEMA flood zone for the address
  • Any elevation certificate on file with the city
  • Roof age and hail or wind repair records
  • Flood or storm insurance claims in the past

sections.h2: What permits and codes apply to a Hobbs house?
sections.html:
The city's Building Safety and Permitting office, part of the Planning and Engineering Department, issues permits for building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work on residential and commercial property. It is at 200 E. Broadway Street, phone (575) 391-8158.

The office lists permits for new buildings, additions, remodels, demolitions, manufactured homes, re-roofs, HVAC, fireplaces, pools, decks, fences and curb cuts. It publishes residential re-roofing guidelines and a homeowner building permit application. Current state codes it lists include the 2021 New Mexico Residential Building Code, effective January 1, 2024.

For a seller, the useful question is whether work done on the house since you bought it had a permit. A buyer's inspector may ask. If you did a re-roof, a deck or a bathroom remodel without paperwork, ask the office what is needed to close the file, or tell a cash buyer up front so the price reflects it. The city's contact page lists Code Enforcement at (575) 391-4178.

Permits outside the city limits need a Lea County address and new construction application first, so confirm whether your property is inside Hobbs before calling.

sections.h2: When are Lea County property taxes due, and who collects them?
sections.html:
New Mexico sets two payment dates statewide: first-half taxes are due November 10 and second-half taxes are due April 10, based on the statute citations in the Doña Ana County Treasurer's calendar. The Lea County Treasurer is the elected tax collector for the county, municipalities, school districts, the State of New Mexico and other taxing entities in Lea County, and prepares and mails bills based on the County Assessor's valuation.

First-half taxes become delinquent after December 10, and second-half taxes after May 10. We did not find a Lea County page with its own list of dates, so check the Treasurer's current notice before you rely on a date.

When a house in Hobbs sells, taxes are a closing item. The title company will ask the Treasurer for the balance, pay what is owed from proceeds, and divide the current year between buyer and seller. If you inherited a house with years of unpaid tax, tell the title company early, since delinquent taxes can lead to a state tax sale after the period set by statute.

sections.h2: How should a Hobbs owner choose between listing and a cash sale?
sections.html:
A listing works best when a house is in good condition, the timeline is flexible and the owner can handle showings and repair requests. A cash sale works best when time or condition is the problem.

Situations that lead owners to consider a direct sale include a job change, a rental with a tenant, an inherited property in a relative's name, or storm damage that insurance did not fully cover. The right choice depends on how much time and money you can spend before closing.

  • Ask each buyer for a written offer and a proposed closing date.
  • Ask who pays title, escrow and recording costs.
  • Confirm the buyer will let the title company handle funds.
  • Do not sign anything that gives a buyer an open-ended option without payment.

We make no promise about a price. Any offer depends on the house, its location and its repair needs.

faqs.q: Is Hobbs in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of the area carry flood risk, and the city says flooding can happen with little warning. Check the FEMA flood map for your address or call the Hobbs Engineering Department at (575) 397-9232, which also keeps elevation certificates.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a building permit in Hobbs?
faqs.a: Call Building Safety and Permitting at (575) 391-8158 at 200 E. Broadway Street. Code Enforcement is listed at (575) 391-4178.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Lea County?
faqs.a: The state calendar sets the first half for November 10 and the second half for April 10, with delinquency after December 10 and May 10. Confirm with the Lea County Treasurer before you pay or close.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hobbs house with a hail-damaged roof?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer usually takes the house in its present condition and prices the roof into the offer. A buyer using a mortgage may ask you to repair it first.

faqs.q: Does the oil industry affect Hobbs house sales?
faqs.a: It affects who is moving in and out. Wikipedia lists oil and gas extraction as the city's largest industry, and the area saw sharp swings in population during earlier booms and busts.

faqs.q: Do I need to fix unpermitted work before selling in Hobbs?
faqs.a: Not always, but a buyer's inspector may ask for permit records. You can ask the city what is needed to close a permit, or sell to a cash buyer who takes the house as is.
